title: Loading Stored Value and Refunding a Till Transaction on an Employee Meal Account
content:
Stored value is loaded in amounts between the smallest and largest single load printed against the plan, and the Employee Meal Account may not be carried above the balance ceiling printed against the same plan; a load that would breach the ceiling is taken down to the amount that fits.

## Automatic reload

Where the plan carries an automatic reload, it fires once the balance falls to the reload threshold printed against the plan and adds the reload amount printed against it, and it fires no more than once in a service day.

## The state the account must stand in

A load or a refund is only made while the account stands active or restricted, since an account that is parked or closed takes no value and an enrolled account has not yet been activated. The account's record settles this before the load or the refund is made, read by the account's own reference alongside the stored value standing on it.

## The refund window

A refund of a till transaction is only made where the request reaches Larkspur Table no later than the refund window for the meal plan, counted in calendar days from the day the till transaction was rung. Refund window days are counted as calendar days from the day after the transaction was rung, every day of the week counts, and a request arriving on the boundary day itself is still in time; calendar days are never converted into full 24-hour periods.

The clock runs from the day the transaction was rung as the transaction itself records it, and the transaction the refund concerns is identified by the till reference printed on it. It is that record, not the employee's recollection of the day, that fixes the anchor.

*Boundary cases, on abstract days.* Where a plan prints a window of a given number of calendar days, a request arriving on the last day of that window is in time, and a request arriving on the day after it is out of time. Counting begins on the day after the transaction was rung, so the day of the transaction itself is not one of the counted days, and weekends and public holidays are counted like any other day.

## Method, floor and allowance-funded transactions

A refund is returned by the method printed against the plan — to stored value, through payroll, or to the card originally used — and never by a method the employee chooses on the day.

A refund smaller than the minimum printed against the plan is not made, and the employee is offered a replacement item instead.

A refund of a transaction that was met from employer allowance restores that allowance rather than paying the employee, and the restored allowance keeps the expiry of the lot it came from rather than starting afresh.
